intro: Here at Andriake, an ancient city in Antalya province from the 2nd century BC, you stand in the harbour of Myra. Its vast granary, built by Hadrian, records the stop this coast made for the grain fleet running from Egypt to Rome.
history: Andriake was the harbour of Myra, and the stop this coast made for the fleet carrying Egyptian grain to Rome. The granary built by Hadrian still stands almost entire, with its eight chambers. And one famous traveller passed this way: Paul changed ships here on his way to Rome.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss Hadrian's granary and the harbour, then the synagogue and the agora.
facts: Did you know? The synagogue excavated at the harbour is one of the best preserved early synagogues found in Anatolia. And the granary Hadrian built still stands almost entire, with its eight chambers.
outro: This brings our tour of Andriake to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Ships once crowded this harbour; now it waits for you to return. Enjoy your visit.
